meta.title: MCO · One review, individual answers
meta.subtitle: Default CLI + built-in shim path · selected providers run independently · source-pinned implementation overview

components.label: 1 · Review CLI
components.explanation: Accepts mco review arguments. Loads configuration defaults and resolves provider selection. Review supplies a natural-language default prompt if none is given; execution mode defaults to read_only, but explicit config/permission overrides can change it. No providers selected is an error, not automatic provider discovery.

components.label: 2 · Validate & plan
components.explanation: Validates target paths against the repository and allow_paths. Builds AgentInvocation records from selected providers and configured models, or explicit [alias=]provider:model declarations. Resolves the adapter registry and rejects unsupported strict policy settings or known-invalid models before executing. The CLI passes the accepted plan, adapters, permissions, context and timeouts to run_invocation_workflow.

components.label: 3 · Invocation scheduler
components.explanation: Without chain, debate or synthesis flags, the workflow directly calls run_invocations. It submits one _run_one_invocation job per declaration, choosing adapters[invocation.provider]. max_provider_parallelism caps workers when positive; otherwise the pool has one worker per invocation. A global deadline and shared cancellation event govern the task. These are local threads, not a distributed queue.

components.label: 4 · Per-invocation worker
components.explanation: Builds TaskInput with prompt, repo root, scope, model and permission metadata. Starts adapter.run under a deadline, then polls the run reference. The worker reads the adapter's stdout log, calls decode_transport, emits output_delta events, and appends answer deltas to the invocation Markdown file. Terminal results retain invocation ID, provider, model, status, output, error and exit code. Failures, cancellation and timeouts remain per-invocation results; the worker requests adapter cancellation when needed.

sources.label: Log read, decoding, deltas and timeout

components.label: Provider shim adapters
components.explanation: The registry maps provider IDs to concrete adapters. In the default built-in shim path, the base adapter spawns the provider CLI with cwd=repo_root and stdout/stderr redirected to local files. poll observes the child process; cancel controls it. Provider overrides construct commands and decode their output formats; Codex is a concrete example, not a required provider. The worker reads these raw log files rather than receiving an HTTP response.

sources.label: Spawn, log capture, poll and cancel

components.label: Selected provider CLIs
components.explanation: Locally launched external CLI executables perform the actual review in the target repository. This boundary is the observed subprocess boundary, not a claim of network or filesystem isolation. Provider-internal model calls, remote hosting and internal review logic are outside the checked-out implementation and are intentionally not invented here.

components.label: 5 · Collect individual results
components.explanation: Futures finish in any order, but the scheduler writes results into their original declaration-index slots. An unexpected worker exception becomes that invocation's failed result. It returns task_id, status, outputs[], exit_code and artifact_root. All successes mean complete/0; some mean partial/1; none mean failed/2. The default path does not merge or synthesize provider answers. Optional persistence writes result.md and run.json, while stdout-only mode uses a temporary directory and clears artifact paths before cleanup.

components.label: 6 · Return to caller
components.explanation: For --json, main prints the final payload with each output's stderr omitted, then returns payload.exit_code. Without --json, the callback renders text deltas labelled by invocation when multiple invocations are active, or prints JSONL lifecycle/output events; diagnostics go to stderr. These streaming callbacks happen during execution, not only after collection. Artifact/both result modes retain files; --save-artifacts promotes stdout to both.

cards.title: One request ≠ one merged answer
items: Selected providers become invocation records; aliases can distinguish multiple models of one provider.
Concurrent completion does not reorder outputs[]. Failure of one invocation can yield a partial task.

cards.title: Local files, optional retention
items: Adapters capture raw stdout/stderr; workers read and decode logs, emit live deltas and write individual Markdown answers.
stdout-only: temporary files cleaned up. artifact/both: retain invocation files, result.md and run.json.

cards.title: Scope & evidence limits
items: This is the default CLI/built-in shim path. ACP/custom transports and opt-in chain, debate and synthesis are not expanded.
Read-only is a configurable permission preset, not a universal isolation guarantee. Provider internals and remote model topology are unknown here.
